title: Longest common subsequence of generated sequences
prompt:
Two sequences A and B of 1000 numbers each are generated like this: start with x = 1 for A (x = 2 for B), and 1000 times replace x with the remainder of x times 75 plus 74, divided by 65537, then append the remainder of x divided by 4 to the sequence. The first 8 numbers of A are 1, 1, 1, 0, 3, 3, 3, 1 and those of B are 0, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1, 3, 2.

A common subsequence of two sequences is a sequence that can be obtained from each of them by deleting elements without changing the order of the rest. The longest common subsequence of the first 8 numbers of A and of B has length 4 (for example 1, 1, 1, 3).

For k = 250, 500, 750 and 1000, print on a line of its own the length of the longest common subsequence of the first k numbers of A and the first k numbers of B.

The running time of the program is measured too, so make it reasonably fast.
